Method of Attack: Hijacking traffic from compromised WordPress sites running vulnerable WordPress CMS version 4.7.1 via remote code execution flaw
Injecting ads on hacked sites to redirect users to Master134 redirection service
Using potentially unwanted programs (PUPs) such as browser homepage hijackers to redirect users
Advertising ad slots on AdsTerra network under a publisher account
Selling ad slots through ad resellers (AdventureFeeds, EvoLeads, ExoClick) to bad actors
Redirecting hijacked traffic to tech support scams, exploit kits, ransomware, banking trojans, and other malware
Impacted Systems: WordPress sites running WordPress CMS version 4.7.1
Attack Vector: Remote code execution vulnerability in WordPress 4.7.1
Malvertising via ad networks and resellers
Indicators of Compromise: AdsTerra advertising network and ad resellers AdventureFeeds, EvoLeads, ExoClick
Traffic purchased by exploit kit operators (RIG, Magnitude, GrandSoft, FakeFlash)
Traffic distribution systems (Fobos, HookAds, Seamless, BowMan, TorchLie, BlackTDS, Slyip)
